title: Extension by zero equals direct image for finite etale module sheaves
statement: Let $\pi:U\to X$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $M$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda_U$-modules on the small etale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The canonical map $c_M:\pi_!M\to\pi_*M$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-to-star-map] from etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] to direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], which is natural in $M$, is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules. This is Stacks Project Lemma 59.70.6, Tag 03S7 (lemma-shriek-equals-star-finite-etale), for module sheaves.

proof.text: *The map.* Write $V_U=V\times_XU$ for an object $V$ of $X_{\Et}$, $p_V:V_U\to V$, $q_V:V_U\to U$ the projections, $P_M$ the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)}M(V,\varphi)$ whose sheafification (as presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules) is $\pi_!M$, with sheafification map $\eta_M:P_M\to\pi_!M$, and $(\pi_*M)(V)=M(V_U)$. The canonical map of the statement is $c_M$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-to-star-map]: the unique morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules with $c_M\circ\eta_M=c^p_M$, where $c^p_{M,V}((s_\varphi)_\varphi)=\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(s_\varphi)$ and $e_\varphi(s)\in M(V_U)$ is the section with $M(\Gamma_\varphi)(e_\varphi(s))=s$ for the graph $\Gamma_\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_V,\varphi):V\to V_U$ that vanishes on $V_U\setminus\Gamma_\varphi(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map]. It is natural in $M$ by the same definition node. So it remains to show that $c_M(W)$ is bijective for every object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), construction of the map; Lemma 03S7 (line 11571) refers to it

proof.text: *Injectivity.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-to-star-injective], $c_M(W):(\pi_!M)(W)\to(\pi_*M)(W)$ is injective for every object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ (Stacks proves this for every separated etale morphism; $\pi$ is finite, hence affine, hence separated).

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), second paragraph of the proof

proof.text: *Etale locally on $X$, $\pi$ is a disjoint union of isomorphisms.* Call an object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$ *split* if there are a finite set $J$ and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j\subseteq T_U$ ($j\in J$) covering $T_U$ such that each $p_T|_{V_j}:V_j\to T$ is an isomorphism. Claim: every object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ has a covering $\{h_x:W_x\to W\}$ in $X_{\Et}$ by split objects. For each $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] (Stacks 04HN) applied to the finite etale $\pi$ and $x$ gives an etale $g_x:X_x\to X$ with $x\in g_x(X_x)$, a finite set $J_x$ and a decomposition $U\times_XX_x=\coprod_{j\in J_x}V_{x,j}$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes such that each $V_{x,j}\to X_x$ (second projection) is an isomorphism. The family $(g_x)_{x\in X}$ is etale and jointly surjective, so the projections $h_x:W_x=W\times_XX_x\to W$ are etale and jointly surjective [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]; $W_x\to W\to X$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(2)], so $W_x$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$, $h_x$ a morphism of $X_{\Et}$, and $\{h_x\}_x$ a covering of $W$ in $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $r_x:W_x\to X_x$ be the second projection. The square with sides $U\times_XX_x\to U$ and $X_x\to X$ is cartesian, so pasting it with the square over $r_x$ [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] identifies $(W_x)_U=W_x\times_XU$, over $W_x$, with $W_x\times_{X_x}(U\times_XX_x)$. Let $V'_j\subseteq(W_x)_U$ be the preimage of $V_{x,j}$ under the projection to $U\times_XX_x$: the $V'_j$ are pairwise disjoint, open and closed, and cover $(W_x)_U$ (preimages of such a family); by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] $V'_j=W_x\times_{X_x}V_{x,j}$ as open subscheme, and its projection to $W_x$ is the base change along $r_x$ of the isomorphism $V_{x,j}\to X_x$, hence an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. So $W_x$ is split.

proof.text: *The split case: surjectivity.* Let $T$ be split by $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ as in step 3, and let $\sigma_j:T\to T_U$ be the inverse of $p_T|_{V_j}$ followed by the inclusion, so $p_T\sigma_j=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $\sigma_j(T)=V_j$. Put $\varphi_j=q_T\sigma_j:T\to U$, an $X$-morphism. Then $\sigma_j=\Gamma_{\varphi_j}$, since both have components $\mathrm{id}_T$ and $\varphi_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; so $\Gamma_{\varphi_j}(T)=V_j$. If $T=\varnothing$ then $T_U=\varnothing$ and $(\pi_*M)(T)=M(\varnothing)=0$, nothing to prove; otherwise the $V_j$ are nonempty and pairwise disjoint, so the $\sigma_j$, hence the $\varphi_j$, are pairwise distinct. Let $t\in(\pi_*M)(T)=M(T_U)$, put $s_j=M(\Gamma_{\varphi_j})(t)\in M(T,\varphi_j)$ and $x=(s_j)_{j\in J}\in P_M(T)$ (the entry $s_j$ in the summand of $\varphi_j$). We show $c^p_{M,T}(x)=\sum_je_{\varphi_j}(s_j)=t$. Fix $k\in J$. For $j\ne k$, $V_k\subseteq T_U\setminus V_j=T_U\setminus\Gamma_{\varphi_j}(T)$, so $e_{\varphi_j}(s_j)$ restricts to $0$ on $V_k$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(2)]. For $j=k$: $e_{\varphi_k}(s_k)$ and $t$ have the same pull-back $s_k$ along $\Gamma_{\varphi_k}$, which is an isomorphism $T\to V_k$ onto the open subscheme $V_k$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map(1)], so their restrictions to $V_k$ agree. Hence $\sum_je_{\varphi_j}(s_j)$ and $t$ have the same restriction to every $V_k$; the inclusions $V_k\to T_U$ are open immersions, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation(1)], jointly surjective, so a covering of $T_U$ in $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $M$ is separated [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], so $\sum_je_{\varphi_j}(s_j)=t$. Therefore $t=c^p_{M,T}(x)=c_M(T)(\eta_M(T)(x))$ (step 1): $c_M(T)$ is surjective for every split $T$. This is the case Stacks omits ('We omit the proof in this case').

source.place: Lemma 03S7 (lemma-shriek-equals-star-finite-etale, line 11571), the split case, whose proof Stacks omits; written out by the worker

proof.text: *Surjectivity in general and conclusion.* Let $W$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ and $t\in(\pi_*M)(W)$. Take a covering $\{h_a:W_a\to W\}$ of $W$ in $X_{\Et}$ by split objects (step 3). By step 4 there are $g_a\in(\pi_!M)(W_a)$ with $c_M(W_a)(g_a)=t|_{W_a}$, the restriction of $t$ along $h_a$ in $\pi_*M$. For indices $a,b$ let $W_{ab}=W_a\times_WW_b$, an object of $X_{\Et}$ and the fibre product there [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits(2)]. As $c_M$ commutes with restrictions, $c_M(W_{ab})(g_a|_{W_{ab}})=t|_{W_{ab}}=c_M(W_{ab})(g_b|_{W_{ab}})$, so $g_a|_{W_{ab}}=g_b|_{W_{ab}}$ by step 2. By the sheaf condition for $\pi_!M$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] there is $g\in(\pi_!M)(W)$ with $g|_{W_a}=g_a$ for all $a$; then $c_M(W)(g)$ and $t$ have the same restriction to every $W_a$, so they are equal, $\pi_*M$ being a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus each $c_M(W)$ is bijective (step 2 and this step) and $\Lambda$-linear; the inverse maps $c_M(W)^{-1}$ are $\Lambda$-linear and commute with the restriction maps (because the $c_M(W)$ do), so they form a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules inverse to $c_M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence $c_M:\pi_!M\to\pi_*M$ is an isomorphism for every $M$, and the natural transformation $c:\pi_!\to\pi_*$ is a natural isomorphism.
